payload.alternatives: Every satellite now, empty ones included: more repositories to keep (CI, Dependabot, security) with nothing in them. Only the monorepo: the presentation pages would wait for a product release. The packages split into repositories of their own: lockstep releases across repositories, and the two readers no longer held in one commit.
payload.rationale: The packages release in lockstep (one version across the nine manifests), depend on each other through workspace:*, the format and both readers (TypeScript and Python) change in one commit, and the required guards read across packages (the packed tarball, the command roster, the host contract, the built-in stack index). Split, each change of format would become a cascade of releases, and the two readers could drift with nobody seeing it. The site and the organization's profile have a cadence of their own; a Marketplace listing for the Action (action.yml at a repository's root) and a Homebrew tap (a homebrew-* repository) are a platform's demand. An empty repository is one more place to keep (CI, Dependabot, security) and nobody else can take a name inside the organization, so none is made ahead of its content.
payload.title: The mnema-work organization holds the product in one repository, mnema, transferred from felipesauer/mnema with its history, and a satellite repository is born only when its lifecycle, release cadence or a platform demand differs from the product, never for tidiness: mnema.work (the site) and .github (the organization profile and default community files) now, action and homebrew-mnema when there is something to put in them; mnema stays the central reference

payload.alternatives: The site stays in the monorepo: one source, but every presentation change waits for the required checks and a release. The docs moved into the site repository: separated from the commands they describe and from the guards that hold them. The release dispatching the site build: a token between repositories.
payload.rationale: Today the site deploys only from a release (site.yml), which is right for the docs, which describe the version npm serves, and wrong for presentation pages, where fixing one sentence would wait for a product release and its 25 required checks. The docs stay where the commands they describe and the guards that hold them live; the site repository takes them from the latest release tag, so the rule that the docs describe the published version holds. A scheduled check of the latest tag instead of a dispatch from the release keeps any token out of both repositories. What the split costs, a docs change that breaks the site build seen only at the next build, is closed by the light check in the product repository.
payload.title: The site moves to its own repository, mnema-work/mnema.work: it holds the presentation pages and the build, deploys its own pages on a push, and builds the docs from docs/ of the latest release tag of mnema, found by a scheduled check so that no token crosses repositories; the docs stay authored in the product repository, where a light check keeps building the docs pages on each pull request; the deploy job keeps holding no secret and running no checkout

payload.alternatives: The apex without the redirect: every homepage already published on npm, the extension and the plugins would answer 404. www as the canonical address: one more hop for the address people type, nothing gained.
payload.rationale: mnema.work is the project's own domain. GitHub Pages does not redirect a transferred repository's site, and npm 0.1.0 to 0.1.5, the VS Code extension and the plugins published felipesauer.github.io/mnema/ as their homepage, which cannot be changed on what is published; once the repository leaves the personal account that path is served by the maintainer's user site, so a page-for-page redirect there keeps every one of them working. The paths map one to one (/mnema/docs/<page> to /docs/<page>). Cloudflare's proxy would stop GitHub from issuing the certificate, so the records stay DNS only. The search engines' verification and the robots file move to mnema.work; the rest of 01a188d1 (titles, descriptions, canonicals, structured data, sitemap) stands.
payload.title: The site is read at https://mnema.work (the presentation), /docs/<page> (the docs of the published version) and /record/ (the record verifier); www redirects to the apex and the DNS records stay DNS only so GitHub issues the certificate; the old address felipesauer.github.io/mnema/ is kept alive by a page-for-page redirect in the maintainer user site, and the search engines are verified on mnema.work

payload.alternatives: work.mnema/mnema by DNS authentication: the brand name, but a private key held as a secret in the npm environment. Keeping io.github.felipesauer/mnema: a workflow in the organization repository is granted the organization namespace, not the old owner one.
payload.rationale: mcp-publisher login github-oidc grants the namespace of the repository's owner: from mnema-work/mnema the workflow is granted io.github.mnema-work/*, and io.github.felipesauer/mnema can no longer be published from it. Keeping OIDC keeps the property the release has today, that no job holds a registry secret. The name changes in server.json, the generator of server.json, the package's mcpName and the release's checks in the same pull request.
payload.title: From the first release after the move, mnema is listed in the official MCP Registry as io.github.mnema-work/mnema, published by the release workflow through GitHub OIDC as before, so the release keeps holding no secret; io.github.felipesauer/mnema stays at 0.1.5 and is marked as replaced where the registry allows it

payload.alternatives: Keeping the two secrets: forgotten credentials that travel with the transfer. Two-factor not required: nothing gained now, and every later member or outside collaborator would join without it. Keeping Mnema AI as the display name: not the brand.
payload.rationale: The organization has one member today, and requiring two-factor authentication costs nothing now and covers every member and outside collaborator later. Its display name follows the brand. The repository secrets NPM_TOKEN and RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN are read by no workflow (npm publishes by trusted publishing, without a token): forgotten credentials that would travel with the transfer; their names, never their values, are kept in the phase 1 snapshot before they go.
payload.title: The mnema-work organization requires two-factor authentication of its members, its display name is Mnema, and the two repository secrets no workflow reads (NPM_TOKEN, RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN) are deleted once the pre-transfer snapshot lists their names

payload.alternatives: No address on the domain: a reporter without a GitHub account has no way in. A security address on the project's own domain gives a reporter without a GitHub account a way in; answering by e-mail from the forwarded inbox would send the maintainer's personal address to the reporter, which ADR-167 forbids, so the conversation continues in GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, already on for the repository. The destination inbox is named nowhere in the repository, the site or the record.

payload.alternatives: Everything allowed (the GitHub default): any action of any owner, by tag, with approval only for a first-time contributor.

A pull request from a fork runs its workflows only once a maintainer approves it, for every outside contributor and not only a first-time one. The default workflow token stays read and Actions cannot approve a review; every workflow declares its own permissions.

payload.alternatives: Raise the timeout to 180 and keep 10 runs: N=30 per night, but nine runners held about 2.5 hours every morning and the pull requests' CI queued behind them. Only Node 24 with 10 runs: loses the comparison between the floor, 24 and 26 that the three Nodes exist for. Turn the night off until the suite is faster: no flake measured meanwhile.
payload.rationale: One run of the suite takes 13.6 minutes on a runner (757 test files, measured on 2026-11-06), so 10 runs per job (about 136 minutes) cannot fit the 90-minute limit and every night since 2026-10-21 was cancelled without a word; 5 runs take about 70 minutes, leaving a margin of 20. A cancelled night opened no issue, which is why seventeen dead nights went unseen. In the organization the free plan shares its runners, and the cron fires hours late (10 to 14 UTC), so a long night holds nine runners during the maintainer's working morning.
payload.title: The flake sampler fits its time limit: a night runs the suite 5 times per job (3 Nodes x 3 shards, N=15 per Node per night), a pull request that touches the sampler runs it once per job to prove it counts, and a night whose ruler breaks (a shard that did not report) opens an issue

The accepted decision on the other tools that rewrite files is to warn, not to edit their configuration (01a15ccf-f2e7).
payload.title: When init finds a Biome configuration that does not leave .mnema/ alone, it ends by saying the exact lines to add (the .mnema folder, and the Copilot instructions file where Biome formats markdown), as mnema doctor already does; init does not edit the Biome configuration

fields.note: Felipe, 2026-11-06, on Biome after init: "O init avisa (Recommended)".

payload.alternatives: Write the block with no blank line: removing it from a file that was empty deletes the file. Record that the file was empty: more machinery than a blank line is worth.
payload.rationale: Without the line, a block that starts at byte 0 cannot be told from a file mnema created, and removing it would delete the file instead of restoring it empty (the-instructions-block.test.ts holds the byte-for-byte removal); a reversible removal is worth more than one cosmetic line.
payload.title: An empty AGENTS.md keeps the blank line the instructions block is written after, so that removing the block gives the file back byte for byte

fields.note: Felipe, 2026-11-06, on the blank line in an empty AGENTS.md: "Manter e fechar (Recommended)".

payload.alternatives: Have an agent read the vendor's public documentation now and correct the text in 0.1.6: a reading of documentation, not of the host, and the release waits for it.
payload.rationale: No test in this repository can decide between a reading of this repository and a reading of a third-party extension; the docs already say the host was never run, so nothing false is printed meanwhile.
payload.title: The two readings of the Antigravity hook are not reconciled in 0.1.6: the code and docs/evidence.md agree (PreToolUse, injectSteps, said as never run on the host), the other words come from a third-party extension, and only a real Antigravity or the vendor's documentation can decide

fields.note: Felipe, 2026-11-06, on the Antigravity readings: "Tirar da 0.1.6 (Recommended)".

payload.alternatives: Rename it to what 0.1.7 is expected to bring: the name and the address change again at each release. Turn it into what 0.1.6 brought: repeats the CHANGELOG and takes the plans out of public view.
payload.rationale: ADR-152 keeps a short public page of what is coming so outsiders see it; with the minimum cut of 0.1.6 (ADR-210) nearly every line of the 0.1.6 page moves past it, and a page named after a version would change its name and its address on the site at every release.
payload.title: The page of what is coming becomes docs/what-comes-next.md, with no version in its name: the plans that 0.1.6 does not carry (the local mode, the backup, the record page redesign, doctor --latest, the proof battery and the rest), each linked to the accepted decision that holds it, at an address that does not change with each release; what 0.1.6 carries is said by the CHANGELOG

fields.note: Felipe, 2026-11-07, on the page of what 0.1.6 brings: "Uma página \"o que vem a seguir\" (Recommended)".

payload.alternatives: Only the low-risk changes (python grouping, found-once-copy): leaves the largest share untouched. maxWorkers=4 first: cheapest, but adds contention against the 5 s ceiling and flakes. Leave it: CI and the flake sampler keep paying 13.6 minutes a run.
payload.rationale: The study of 2026-11-07 put about 81% of a run in child processes and measured about 0.15 s of each built-CLI start in the ESM loader, but the spawn count is an estimate (3,000 to 6,000); the bundle is the largest and riskiest change and also changes what users run, so it waits for the count; grouping the python3 calls is low risk and keeps each case's assertion.
payload.title: The suite's time is attacked by measuring first: count the child processes a whole run starts, by kind, before any change to how the CLI is built; if the built CLI's start-up is confirmed as the largest share, a study of a bundled dist/cli.js follows, since it would speed up the suite and every hook and MCP start a user pays; meanwhile the second reader's python3 calls are grouped into few processes

fields.note: Felipe, 2026-11-07, on where to start with the suite's time: "Medir e depois a partida (Recommended)".

payload.alternatives: Bundle only the workspace code, dependencies left in node_modules: each dependency stays installed and checked by npm audit signatures and its license as it is, but the hook gains about half as much (292 to 184 ms) and the MCP a quarter (384 to 283 ms); the orchestrator recommended it for the proof criterion and the maintainer chose otherwise. A single file without chunks: node:sqlite is linked before the floor check runs. Node's compile cache alone: small, only from the second run, and writes a cache on the user's machine. Not now: the suite and every start stay as they are.
payload.rationale: The study of 2026-11-07 measured the start of every verb, hook and MCP at about half of today's (--version 193 to 97 ms, the hook 292 to 130, MCP initialize 384 to 204), and the built CLI is 60% of the suite's worker time; with everything inside the hooks and the MCP gain the most. Accepted cost: the bundled dependencies become code of the mnema package, covered by its own provenance and no longer by npm audit signatures of each dependency, which the docs must say; a third-party notices file is required; stack traces name chunks.
payload.title: The CLI ships as an esbuild bundle of dist/cli.js with everything inside (the workspace and its third-party dependencies, except string-width and react-devtools-core), split into chunks so the Node floor check runs before any other import, not minified, emitted beside the tsc output, maps not published; built and guarded in one pull request, the bin switched with a third-party notices file and the docs in a second

fields.note: Felipe, 2026-11-07, between bundling only mnema's code (recommended) and everything inside: "Tudo dentro".

payload.alternatives: A stamp file the build writes and both builds read: a new file in dist and a read at every start, for no gain over the constant.
payload.rationale: One stamp keeps a projection cache valid across both builds, nothing new is written to dist, and the run from source is unchanged; in a bundle the files productStamp hashed do not exist and decision record, brief and site died on ENOENT.
payload.title: The bundled CLI gets the product stamp of its cache as a build-time constant (an esbuild define) equal to the stamp the compiled core computes from the same files; the tsc build and the tests keep hashing the files

payload.alternatives: Emit the bundle at a depth where the relative paths happen to hold: true by coincidence and only for some of them. A fallback to the module-relative path: an uncovered branch no install reaches.
payload.rationale: The same module runs from src, dist and dist/bundle at different depths, so no relative path is true in all three; in the bundle the relative package.json of the floor check did not exist and Node 20 and 24.14 ran past the floor into a stack trace.
payload.title: The package's own files are named from the package root, found by walking up to the package.json named @mnema/code (src/package-root.ts), by the Node floor check, the site verifier and the stack index; it throws when no root is found

payload.alternatives: Chunks directly in dist/: the entry's name collides with the compiled cli.js.
payload.rationale: Beside the tsc output without colliding with dist/cli.js, which the bin still names until the second pull request; maps are not published today.
payload.title: The bundle is emitted at packages/code/dist/bundle/ (the entry cli.js and its chunks), carried by the existing dist/ entry of the package's files, with no source maps and with the dependencies' legal comments kept
